dedupe_keys.name: building with nature indonesia demak mangrove restoration for coastal protection

description: Building with Nature Indonesia is a coastal protection programme on the muddy, eroding coast of Demak in Central Java, where more than 3 km of land and whole villages have been lost to the sea through removal of mangrove belts for aquaculture, coastal infrastructure that disturbs sediment supply, and groundwater extraction that causes subsidence. It was led by Wetlands International with EcoShape, the Indonesian ministries of marine affairs and fisheries and of public works, Witteveen+Bos, Deltares, Wageningen University and Research, Diponegoro University and others, funded among others by the Dutch Sustainable Water Fund and Germany's International Climate Initiative. Started as a small pilot in 2013 and run as a five-year programme from 2015 to 2020, it built permeable brushwood and bamboo dams that trap sediment so that mangroves regenerate naturally as a living flood defence, combined with sustainable aquaculture that gives ponds back to mangroves and with community development plans. Scenario maps contrast a 2030 business-as-usual flooding of villages with a restored coastline; sea level rise is projected to flood 6 km inland by 2100, affecting over 70,000 people. The project pages are accessible online as free HTML on the EcoShape website. Caveats: the pages report progress qualitatively, and subsidence must be solved for lasting results. It is an example of design and retrofit of green infrastructure for coastal flood adaptation and relates to Global Mangrove Watch data and ecosystem service models such as InVEST.
